level_1: Demonstrates understanding of the anatomy and physiology of the middle and inner ear, as well as common causes of pediatric and adult hearing loss

level_2: Demonstrates basic understanding of comprehensive audiologic testing (e.g., pure tone audiometry, speech testing, immittance testing)
Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of the pathophysiology of cochlear hearing loss

Demonstrates understanding of indications, outcomes, risks, and complications of cochlear implantation in patients with temporal bone abnormalities and advanced surgical reconstruction of aural atresia
level_3: Demonstrates basic understanding of non- surgical and surgical options for aural rehabilitation
Demonstrates understanding of the medical and surgical management of conductive, mixed, and sensory-neural hearing loss
Conducts original research related to hearing loss
level_4: Demonstrates proficient knowledge of normal and abnormal temporal bone and cochleovestibular histopathology

level_5: Lists unusual causes for hearing loss in pediatric and adult patients, and orders/interprets appropriate advanced audiometric, laboratory, and imaging studies

level_2: Lists common causes of peripheral and central vertigo

level_4: Describes the integration of the peripheral vestibular system with other sensory and motor systems (e.g., vision, proprioception)
Demonstrates knowledge of physical therapy and other rehabilitative options for peripheral and central vestibular disorders
Develops a course or conference related to dizziness for a regional or national meeting
level_5: Differentiates otologic from non-otologic causes of vertigo
Demonstrates comprehensive understanding and interpretation of advanced vestibular testing
Demonstrates understanding of indications, outcomes, risks, and complications of emerging technology, including vestibular implants

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment model
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems, including government, private, public, uninsured care, and practice models
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transitions of care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how they impact patient care
Advocates for patient care needs (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources) with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model
level_4: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type)
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transitions of care
level_5: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Participates in health policy advocacy activities

level_1: Demonstrates how to access available evidence, and incorporates patient preferences and values to take care of routine neurotologic conditions
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to manage complex neurotologic conditions
level_4: Critically appraises the current literature and presents management in either a grand rounds or journal club setting
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan, and, when necessary, improves it
level_3: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Intentionally seeks performance data consistently, with adaptability
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for lapses in professionalism

level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care
Recognizes situations that might trigger lapses in professionalism and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations and how to appropriately report lapses in professionalism
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed
level_4: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations

level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that might impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Gives appropriate feedback to individuals or groups to facilitate task completion in a timely manner
level_4: Recognizes situations that might impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Leads a conference on accountability and task completion
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

subcompetencies.name: Knowledge of Systemic and Individual Factors of Well-Being

level_1: Recognizes the importance of getting help when needed to address personal and professional well-being
Recognizes the institutional factors affecting well-being
level_2: Recognizes departmental factors affecting well-being
Reflects on actions in real time to proactively respond to the inherent emotional challenges of physician work
level_3: Lists resources to support personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional factors that affect one’s own well-being and that of others
level_4: Participates in departmental well-being committee activities
Participates in institutional changes to promote personal and professional well-being
level_5: With prompting, reflects on how personal and professional well-being can impact one’s clinical practice
Suggests potential solutions to institutional factors that affect well- being

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport

Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability) while accurately communicating one’s own role within the health care system

When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information; elicits a patient’s/patient’s family’s values, goals, and preferences; and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Role models self- awareness while identifying a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy)

level_4: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
Facilitates teaching of team-based communication and feedback
level_5: Respectfully receives feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Facilitates health care team-based feedback in routine situations

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record
